title: Giant Stone Statue
text: “Uh… I’d really rather you didn’t make one of those.”
“Depending on the tourist spot, some places carve heroes’ faces into mountainsides. Voff.”
“Shieldfreeden has one too. Apparently there was one of Takt’s face, but once his misdeeds came to light, they tore it down.”
“There’s one there too, huh… There was something like that in my old world as well.”
“There’s one in mine too, I say. I’ve even gone to see it, indeed.”

It was quite a sight, so I think it would serve well to demonstrate Father’s authority. Come to think of it, I believe I once heard a rumor that if the Spirit Tortoise failed to revive, there was talk of that country planning, as part of some public works project, to build a statue of their king. I’ve never actually seen the finished result, though. That’s about as much as I can vaguely recall, I say.
“Those can be made fairly cheap. Just carve away a mountainside.”
“Really?”
“Voff, someone who can use earth magic does it.”

“I see… true, magic does exist. But I don’t want a giant stone statue of myself. It’s scary to think what Imiya-chan and the others would build if they found out… ah, that’s it, maybe I should preemptively have them make a statue of Itsuki instead.”

Seems he doesn’t want a statue of himself, so he’s leaning toward having one of Itsuki made instead. Come to think of it, Cal Mira Island also had stone statues, since it was a training ground passed down from the heroes. I recall seeing one at the temple of wish-granting. Generally speaking, across most loops there’s no stone statue of Shield Hero, though. Or rather, one was in the process of being made, I say. Apparently it had been destroyed long ago due to the Three Heroes Church’s influence, and restoration work was underway.
“Iwatani-sama, you really do come up with some rather sinister ideas sometimes.”
Rabbit Guy said something like that.
“Ha ha ha.”
Father just laughed and let the matter slide.
“Any other interesting rooms around?”
“Voff—there was a room I prepared for brother’s sake, for making fatigue-recovery medicine, but… I’m bad at that stuff now, so please spare me.”
“Ah, right, Wolf isn’t great with medicine—or rather, alchemy in general, huh… well, can’t help that.”
“Mixing basic medicine is fine, it’s just… Wo, Wo… Kyaiin kyaiin!?”
For some reason, as Wolf tried to remember something, he turned to look at my face, then suddenly let out a scream as if panicking.
“Wh-Wolf!? What’s wrong? Calm down!”
“Kyaiin kyaiin!? Ugh… ah, I-I’m fine. Meatballs came to mind for some reason, but I’m okay.”
“Meatballs? Right, Wolf really does hate those. He’s recovered his energy, but trauma isn’t something you overcome so easily, huh.”
Crocodile Guy and the others watched Wolf with somewhat puzzled expressions, silently observing the exchange with Father. How pitiful of Wolf.
“Anyway, looks like I’ll be imposing on this place for a little while. I’ll enjoy the local specialties and everything.”
“P-please take your time and enjoy our home to the fullest, voff!”
And so, checking out the notable rooms of Wolf’s residence came to something of a close, I say.
“Come to think of it, in good old-fashioned RPGs, heroes go treasure-hunting through castles, opening chests and searching rooms… well, I never did that in Melromarc or Siltvelt though.”
“Ah, pilfering equipment! There’s copying too, so it’s not a bad strategy at all, I say!”
“True enough. I did copy weapon categories in Siltvelt, Faubrey, and Melromarc, after all.”
“Voff, quite a few different nobles have weapons handed down from past heroes.”

“I’ve seen plenty of that myself across the loops, indeed. Sometimes there are shiny things, but true masterpieces are rare. The overly powerful ones tend to have vanished… no, mostly they’ve been stolen and their whereabouts lost, I say.”
Commonly, they’re mostly found in this world’s hidden dungeons. Since it’s not a problem to go without them, it often gets put off for later.
“Above all, the weapons obtained from dungeons like Cal Mira Island are more than sufficient, I say.”
“I suppose so. The gear that came out of there was pretty impressive—not having to hunt around elsewhere is nice, I guess.”
“That’s a rather dangerous topic to be discussing. Though… it would help the other heroes as well…”
“Tricky balance, that.”
“We definitely shouldn’t do that though—if our equipment wasn’t up to par, maybe it’d be something to consider, but that’s well within the realm of basic morality, right?”
When the topic of stealing came up, Father and the others firmly said to leave such things be. So there’s no need to even bring it up further, I say.
“Well, even so, isn’t searching around for things without being given anything just part of being a gamer?”
“Our treasury doesn’t have much in the way of precious metals that could quickly be turned into cash.”
“Huh, is that so. Come to think of it, wolf-men don’t care much for silver, do they?”
“Silver? Once you reach the head-of-household class, due to fur coloring it doesn’t stand out much, so other things are preferred instead.”
“Come to think of it, Wolf, your coloring did turn silvery. So silver-on-silver is a bit awkward, huh.”

And so, chatting away like that, the exploration of Wolf’s castle wrapped up for the time being, I say. Since it wasn’t a hot spring resort, bathing was done in a regular bathhouse, and since it was all men in the bath, all I could do was peek to boost Yuki-chan’s charm. Panda was in there too, indeed.
“Voff!”

After bathing, Wolf strolled about the castle in a bathrobe, keeping Father company. Crocodile Guy and the others seemed intent on making sure Father was never left alone with Wolf in the head of household’s room for some reason.
And so, as the sun set, dinner time arrived, and everyone gathered in the castle garden to eat, I say.
“Voff! To celebrate Shield Hero-sama’s visit, I, Magarum, who became Claw Hero, and the head of household named Wolf by Hero-sama, hereby declare! Cheers!”
“Cheers!!!”

The servants and people of the territory had come out to the garden as if for a welcome party, offering a Siltvelt-style celebration toward Father seated at the guest table. Looking a bit nervous, Father lightly raised a hand in response. Incidentally, since Wolf and the others were keeping a watchful eye, no one was permitted to approach carelessly, and the range within which people could approach was clearly defined, so the meal wasn’t interrupted.
“This is Siltvelt too, huh. Guess they’d throw a spectacle-like welcome party.”
Looking a bit troubled, Father waved lightly at the townsfolk while enjoying the meal. Wolf, too, was going around greeting the nobles who’d come from nearby, introducing Father to them.
“At least there’s no room given for anyone to pull anything strange.”
“True. Though… I have to admit, it’s frustrating when people talk fast and I can’t catch what they’re saying. There are some accents I just can’t parse.”
“Yeah… honestly, there are times I have no idea what’s being said. The Siltvelt castle dialect is still easier to follow, painfully enough. Larsazusa, Elmelo, can you two understand it?”
“Ahh? Well… I can understand it just fine.”
“In my case, I sometimes get stuck.”

Seems this region’s dialect isn’t something everyone can fully keep up with. While thinking that, I noticed some section of the grounds seemed to be getting rather lively, so I went to check it out, only to find some kind of event going on where people were throwing something like darts at a poster of a pig.
“Hahaha! Take that!”
“How dare you do that to Magarum-sama and Ruhabert-sama!”
“Voff… going out of your way to prepare something like that for entertainment makes me question your taste. Stop it.”
Looking displeased, Wolf scolded them for the game of skewering a pig poster with darts.
“O-our deepest apologies!”
The one who’d been leading the activity bowed their head repeatedly to Wolf. Hmm… a game of skewering a pig with darts, is it. That is indeed rather tasteless, I say.
“Well… it’s not too different from something like the training ground Itsuki made, so it doesn’t leave the best impression on me either.”
Watching that exchange unfold, Father came over near me and murmured, more or less in passing.
